judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'Simplifique!' link in the standard gov.br federal bar, next to 'Comunica BR', 'Participe', 'Acesso à informação' and similar links. The text is the proper name of the federal Simplifique! service that the link points to, so it names the destination, in the same way a nav link named after its target page does (G91). The finding wants the text to explain what the program is, which goes beyond 2.4.4. On the live check (2026-10-28) the old economia URL now leads to a login-restricted 'Conteúdo Restrito' page. That makes it a broken or outdated link, which is not a 2.4.4 failure of the link text.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is a 'Leia mais...' link in the 'Nota de pesar' news card. The DOM is li > article > p > a, and the enclosing list item holds the h3 'Nota de pesar', the date and the summary about Adriana Vidotte. That is programmatically determined link context (H77, enclosing list item; H80, preceding heading), so the link's purpose can be determined and 2.4.4 passes. The packet's ancestors show this context, so the claim that nothing around the link tells where it goes is wrong.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The icon-only 'Rádio UFG' link in the header has no visible text. It is a white radio glyph on a 34px circle filled with #66aad5. I measured the screenshot pixels: #66aad5 and #ffffff, 2.54:1. The circle is also 2.54:1 against the white page, so nothing that identifies the control reaches 3:1. The fill comes from the site's own .social-icon style, not from any brand, so no exception applies, and the 1.4.11 failure is real.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the news-card image for 'Informe à comunidade acadêmica' and the only content of its link. Its alt is 'INFORME_capa.png', so the browser's accessible name for the link is that file name; the title only supplies the description. The image shows the word 'Informe', but the alt is clearly a file name with its extension, which is F30. As a functional image, it also does not describe the link's purpose. Even if it were treated as decorative, a non-empty file-name alt would still fail 1.1.1.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'Ser UFG' button in the left side dock: a white heart icon on a #66aad5 pill, measured at 2.54:1 from the screenshot. The span 'Ser UFG' is in the DOM, but the live CSS sets .side-dock .btn>span to opacity:0 unless the button is .active. Hover only darkens the background, and the screenshot shows the button as an icon only. So at rest the icon is the only visual identifier and it needs 3:1. It fails.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is a carousel banner that is the sole content of a link to the Propessoas Estágio Probatório news item. The image carries a lot of text: 'Atenção servidores técnico-administrativos e docentes ingressantes após 07/02/2025', the MGI/SouGOV notice, and 'Clique aqui e saiba mais'. Its alt is the file name 'banner_-_Estágio_Probatório_novo.png', which also becomes the link's accessible name; the title is only the description. That is a file-name text alternative (F30) that conveys neither the banner's text nor its function, so 1.1.1 fails.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the icon-only Twitter link in the footer: a white bird glyph on a #66aad5 circle, on white. Measured at 2.54:1 from the screenshot. Logos are exempt only when the low-contrast look is the brand's own; here the colour is the site's uniform .social-icon fill, also used for the non-brand radio and TV icons, so it is the author's choice. The Understanding document says such logos are not exempt. The icon is the only identifier, so 1.4.11 fails.

judgments.label: true_positive

The 1.4.11 failure holds.

judgments.label: true_positive

The link is an active, working control rather than an inactive one, and it is neither a logo nor decorative, so no exception applies. 1.4.3 fails.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This h3 is the headline of a Jornal UFG card. Under it are the kicker 'COVID-19' and the deck 'Pesquisa da UFG mostra o poder do testemunho frente aos traumas da linha de frente da pandemia'. 'Relembrar para não repetir' (remember so as not to repeat) is the article's own title, and it describes the same story the deck summarises: remembering pandemic trauma through testimony. A journalistic headline that matches its teaser describes its topic. Nothing under it is a different topic, so 2.4.6 is not failed.
